title: The Last Cookie

before.title: The Last Cookie
before.text:
There is one cookie on the plate. Ali wants it. His sister wants it too.

Ali takes a knife and cuts the cookie in two. He gives one part to his sister.

She says, "Thank you."

Ali says, "We can make more tomorrow." They eat and smile.

after.title: The Last Cookie
after.text:
There is one cookie on the plate. Ali wants it. His sister wants it too.

Ali breaks the cookie in two with his hands. He gives half to his sister.

She says, "Thank you."

Ali says, "We can make more tomorrow." They eat and smile.

reason: Replaced the knife with breaking the cookie by hand. Half clearly refers to one of two pieces. The sharing and final line remain in the same present-tense sequence.

title: The Blue Umbrella

before.title: The Blue Umbrella
before.text: Rain starts when Emi leaves the shop. She has no umbrella. A man by the door has a big blue one. He says, "We can walk together." They go to the bus stop. Emi stays dry. When the bus comes, she waves. The man waves back.

after.title: The Blue Umbrella
after.text:
Rain starts when Emi leaves the shop. She has no umbrella. Her friend Ken is by the door. He has a big blue umbrella.

Ken says, "Let’s walk to the bus stop." They walk together. Emi stays dry.

When her bus comes, she waves to Ken. He waves back.

reason: Identified Ken as Emi’s friend before he offers to share his umbrella; the bus arrival and goodbye now clearly follow their walk. The umbrella remains the key concrete image.

title: A Note in the Lunch Box

before.title: A Note in the Lunch Box
before.text: Jun opens his lunch box. There is rice, an egg, and a small note. The note says, "Have a good day." Jun reads it two times. At home, he puts a note by his mother's cup. It says, "Have a good day too."

after.title: A Note in the Lunch Box
after.text:
Jun opens his lunch box. There is rice, an egg, and a small note. The note says, "Have a good day." Jun reads it again.

At home, Jun writes a note for his mother. He puts it by her cup. It says, "Thank you, Mom."

reason: Changed two times to reads it again and gave Jun a natural reply to his mother. His new note and its place are explicit, preserving the kind exchange.
